annotation.evidence_span: unless it is protected from an infinite request loop
annotation.interpretation_a: The intermediary must have a mechanism to detect and prevent forwarding messages back to itself, effectively breaking any potential loop.
annotation.interpretation_b: The intermediary can forward messages to itself if it has some external protection mechanism (e.g., a rate limiter, a hop limit) that prevents an infinite loop, even if the intermediary itself doesn't actively detect the loop.
annotation.justification: The phrase 'protected from an infinite request loop' is vague. It doesn't specify *how* an intermediary must be protected, leaving room for different implementations. One implementation might actively detect loops, while another might rely on external mechanisms. This difference in implementation behavior constitutes ambiguity.
annotation.missing_information: The definition of 'protected from an infinite request loop' is not specified. What constitutes sufficient protection is unclear and affects implementation.
